subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1390 landed (wave 68 s). Printed format (PDF p233): relation-condition-1 { {AND|OR|EXCLUSIVE-OR|XOR} {NOT|simple-relational-operator|extended-relational-operator} object-1 } ... — ONE group, any connective in any position (cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.2 "relation-condition-1" OK; --check 8.8.4.12.1 "any relation condition except the first may be abbreviated by" OK). The grammar now spells the tail ONCE: the leading tiers hold the first simple condition and every connective's operand (OR, XOR, AND alike) is a succeeding tier whose leftmost element is succeedingCondition = abbreviatedRelation | unaryLogicalExpression; the EVALUATE partial spine uses the same succeeding tails. Probed on the w68s build: A = B OR < C AND D -> F, OR < C AND NOT D -> T, A = B XOR < C -> T, XOR NOT < C -> F, OR < C XOR = D -> F, OR < D AND C = 1 -> F, A = 1 XOR = 2 -> T (all were COBOL0001/0901). Goldens run each shape over all 81 tuples of A..D in 1..3 against the GR1 expansion: 0 disagreements. The connective '(' after XOR / EXCLUSIVE-OR (e.g. A = B XOR (C + 1)) is still mis-lexed as a subscript opener — the lexer's edition-blind subscript trigger, kb/Work PB1162, which owns FMT-8.8.4.11.2 (the connective row); it fails before any rule of this clause is reached. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4#abbreviatedAndChain (kb/Work PB1390 deleted the OR-only abbreviatedAndChain rule; its job is the succeeding tiers, now witnessed on this row) Re-affirmed 2026-10-22 (kb/Work PB3530) against the figure regenerated from the printed page: render_figure.py's brace-group layout now keeps every alternative inside its own enclosure, so the diagram's layout changed while its words did not (sweep_figures.py's word gate); the verdict stands on the printed format.
